title: Dragster: Drive and light the way
footnote: Use Bricks4Kidz motors and an eight-LED NeoPixel strip on P16 in RGB (GRB) mode. Lift the wheels for bench tests. The basic driving program has no stop button.

reference.source: Session 30. Dragster.pdf, physical PDF pages 15-18. Motor code on page 15; matching light code on page 18. Combined without added commands.
notes: Retain both explicit strip.show() calls from the PDF, even though showColor also sends the strip data.
The reference has no pause, motor stop, or running guard. Repeated A presses send the same two motor values again.
Light level exactly 100 uses the else branch (white). On first use the light API returns 0 before the sensor is ready.

stages.title: Button A controls one motor
stages.concept: A button event sends a motor command.
stages.adds: Intermediate: add on button A pressed and DC motor A power 100.
stages.predict: Which motor will start when A is pressed?
observe: Press A: motor A is commanded to 100.
Motor B has no command yet.
Another press sends 100 again.
stages.question: Does this program ever tell motor A to stop?
stages.run: Download this intermediate program. Lift the wheels, press A briefly, then disconnect motor power before changing the build.

stages.title: Drive both wheels forward
stages.concept: Opposite motor signs suit motors facing opposite directions.
stages.adds: Keep motor A at 100. Add motor B at -100 inside the same Button A event.
stages.predict: Will opposite signs move the car forward?
observe: A sends 100 to A and -100 to B.
Both wheels drive the car forward.
There is still no stop command.
stages.question: Why does motor B need the opposite sign?
stages.run: Download and lift the wheels first. Press A and check both wheel directions; then test forward motion in a clear area. Disconnect motor power to stop the car.

stages.title: Connect the eight lights
stages.concept: A variable stores the NeoPixel strip connection.
stages.adds: Keep Button A. In on start, set strip to P16, 8 LEDs, RGB (GRB), then show white.
stages.predict: Will the lights wait for Button A?
observe: At startup the eight LEDs show white.
A still sends the two motor commands.
The lights are not light-controlled yet.
stages.question: Which blocks belong in on start?
stages.run: Connect the eight-LED strip to P16. Download and reset; check the external strip before pressing A.
stages.focusNote: Excerpt: add these on-start blocks; keep the paired Button A motor program unchanged.

stages.title: Read the surrounding light
stages.concept: A forever loop repeatedly reads the light level.
stages.adds: Keep the motors and white strip. Add a forever loop that shows the light level on the micro:bit display.
stages.predict: Will covering the LED display lower the reading?
observe: The display scrolls changing light readings.
Cover or uncover the display and compare.
The external strip remains white.
stages.question: Why must the sensor be read repeatedly?
stages.run: Download, then cover and uncover the micro:bit LED display. Wait for each number to finish scrolling. Motor checks still need the physical build.
stages.focusNote: Intermediate excerpt: add this forever loop. Keep Button A and the existing strip setup.

stages.title: Drive with automatic lights
stages.concept: An if/else chooses the lights from the current light level.
stages.adds: Replace the number display and startup white command with light control: above 100, show black; otherwise, show white. Keep Button A unchanged.
stages.predict: At light level 100, will the strip be white?
observe: Above 100: the strip is black (off).
At 100 or below: it shows white.
A still sends motor A 100 and B -100.
stages.question: Which branch runs when the light level is 100?
stages.run: Download. Cover and uncover the display to cross the threshold. Test Button A separately with the wheels raised. Reset and repeat the checks.
stages.focusNote: Loop excerpt only: keep the P16 eight-LED strip setup and Button A motor event. See Full program for all blocks.

stages.title: Try an idea: a stop button
stages.concept: A second event can stop both motors.
stages.adds: Start with the complete driving and lighting program. Add Button B with motor A 0 and motor B 0.
stages.predict: What should B do after A starts the motors?
observe: A starts both motors at 100 and -100.
B sends 0 to both motors.
The light loop continues independently.
stages.question: Why should B stop both motors?
stages.run: Download with the wheels raised. Press A, then B; repeat A-B to check restart and stop. The external light strip should still react.
stages.focusNote: Add a separate Button B event to stop both motors. Keep the existing light-control loop.

stages.title: Try an idea: compare power
stages.concept: A fair test changes motor power while keeping distance fixed.
stages.adds: Optional variation: keep the stop button; change A to 50 and B to -50 in the launch event.
stages.predict: Will half power give exactly half the speed?
observe: A sends 50 to A and -50 to B.
B still stops both motors.
Compare travel time on the same track.
stages.question: What must stay the same for a fair comparison?
stages.run: Compare this 50-power version with the full-power version over the same marked distance. Use the same surface and battery; stop with B.
stages.focusNote: Set the launch power to 50/-50 and keep Button B stop. Keep the light-control program unchanged.

stages.title: Try an idea: a one-second run
stages.concept: A pause holds the sequence before the stop commands.
stages.adds: Optional variation: after 50/-50, add pause 1000 ms, then set both motors to 0. Keep Button B stop.
stages.predict: Which command comes after the one-second pause?
observe: A starts a one-second command sequence.
After the pause, both motors receive 0.
B can send 0 before the pause ends.
stages.question: Does the pause turn the motors off by itself?
stages.run: Press A once and wait for the timed stop before pressing A again. Check B during a run. This simple version has no running guard; avoid starting another run before the previous one finishes.
stages.focusNote: Replace the launch event with this timed version. Keep Button B stop and the light-control loop.

stages.title: Try an idea: adjust the threshold
stages.concept: The threshold changes when the headlights switch on.
stages.adds: Start with the complete driving and lighting program. Change only the light threshold from 100 to 150.
stages.predict: At light level 120, will the lights turn on?
observe: Above 150: the strip is off.
At 150 or below: it is white.
At 120, it now takes the white branch.
stages.question: How does a higher threshold change the response?
stages.run: Test the same locations with threshold 100, then 150. Compare where the strip changes. Keep motor A at 100 and motor B at -100 for this experiment.
stages.focusNote: Loop excerpt only: keep the P16 eight-LED strip setup and Button A motor event. See Full program for all blocks.
